title: Is AI Really Destroying the Planet?
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 哈喽，哈喽，哈喽，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 制作的英语学习播客《English Learning for Curious Minds》。在这个节目里，你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上稀奇古怪而又美妙的事物，同时还能提高你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about Artificial Intelligence and the environment.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们要聊的是人工智能与环境。

sentences.en: It has been billed as a disaster in plain sight, technology pointlessly destroying the planet, but is there actually any substance behind it?
sentences.zh: 它被贴上了“众目睽睽之下的灾难”和“毫无意义地毁灭地球的技术”的标签，但它的背后真的有什么实质内容吗？

sentences.en: Why are some environmental activists highly critical of things like ChatGPT?
sentences.zh: 为什么一些环保活动人士对 ChatGPT 之类的事物持高度批判态度？

sentences.en: Are they right to be critical, and what does this all mean for you?
sentences.zh: 他们的批判有道理吗？这一切对你意味着什么？

sentences.en: OK then, let's not waste a minute and get right into it.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们废话少说，马上切入正题。

sentences.en: There was a report from BBC Scotland a few weeks ago with the title “Scottish data centres powering AI already using enough water to fill 27 million bottles a year”.
sentences.zh: 几周前，BBC 苏格兰频道报道了一篇新闻，标题是《支持 AI 的苏格兰数据中心每年消耗的水量已足够装满 2700 万瓶》。

sentences.en: The headline was deliberately provocative.
sentences.zh: 这个标题显然带有煽动性。

sentences.en: 27 million bottles sounds like…a lot. And if AI is responsible for using all of this, does this mean 27 million fewer bottles of water for the good people of Scotland?
sentences.zh: 2700 万瓶听起来……很多。如果 AI 消耗了所有这些水，这是否意味着苏格兰的好心人们就要少喝 2700 万瓶水了？

sentences.en: For the story, the reporter had taken to the streets to ask people whether they used tools like ChatGPT, and whether they knew “it could be bad for the environment”, using that exact phrasing of the sentence.
sentences.zh: 为了这篇报道，记者走上街头，用这句话的原意询问人们是否使用 ChatGPT 之类的工具，以及是否知道“它可能对环境有害”。

sentences.en: A loaded question, as we say in English.
sentences.zh: 用我们英语里的话说，这是一个带有诱导性的问题。

sentences.en: Of course, most said they were not, and agreed that people should be more aware of it.
sentences.zh: 当然，大多数人都说他们不知道，并认同人们应该对此有更多认识。

sentences.en: And the general reaction is probably best summed up by the end of the clip, where an elderly gentleman commented, “one day you’re waking up and you cannae have a shower because there’s no water because it’s cooling down some computer somewhere”.
sentences.zh: 片段结尾处的一位老绅士的评论大概最能总结大众的普遍反应，他评论道：“有一天你醒来，却没法洗澡了，因为没有水了，水都被拿去冷却某个地方的电脑了。”

sentences.en: So, is this actually true? Are the good people of Scotland in danger of having to go without a shower because the water has all been used for your and my ChatGPT queries?
sentences.zh: 所以，这真的是真的吗？苏格兰的好心人们真的面临没水洗澡的危险吗？因为水全都被你我的 ChatGPT 查询给用光了？

sentences.en: In a word, no, especially not in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，并没有，苏格兰尤其不可能。

sentences.en: As one user on Facebook humorously put it, “I live in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 正如 Facebook 上的一位用户幽默地指出的那样：“我住在苏格兰。

sentences.en: I often think “if only we had more water, I mean if just for once it could fall out of the sky or something.
sentences.zh: 我经常想‘要是我们有更多水就好了，我是说如果哪怕有那么一次它能从天上掉下来或者怎么着就好了。

sentences.en: I’m burning up here””. To be fair, if you clicked into the BBC article and didn’t just watch the video, the article did admit that water use for data centres had increased significantly, but was still only responsible for 0.005% of the water supply in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 我这热得不行了’”。说实话，如果你点进那篇 BBC 的文章，而不只是看了那个视频，你就会发现文章确实承认了数据中心的水资源消耗显著增加，但它依然只占苏格兰供水量的 0.005%。

sentences.en: And anyone who lives in Scotland or who has visited Scotland will probably be able to tell you, without reaching for any official dataset or doing complicated calculations on Excel, that Scotland has many problems, but water does not seem to be one of them; if Scotland were an independent country, it would be the second wettest country in Europe.
sentences.zh: 任何住在苏格兰或去过苏格兰的人大概都能告诉你，根本不需要查阅什么官方数据集或在 Excel 里做复杂的计算：苏格兰有很多问题，但水似乎不是其中之一；如果苏格兰是一个独立的国家，它将是欧洲降水第二多的国家。

sentences.en: So, as far as Scotland is concerned, they could build 100 times as many data centres, and it would still only use 0.5% of the Scottish water supply, and that’s assuming there are no improvements in efficiency in how this water is used.
sentences.zh: 所以，就苏格兰而言，他们就算建造多达 100 倍的数据中心，也只会消耗苏格兰供水量的 0.5%，而且这还是假设这些水的使用效率没有任何提升的前提下。

sentences.en: Now, before we get into some of the details of the other environmental concerns around AI, it’s first worth spending a few minutes clarifying exactly what we’re talking about, how AI uses energy, and why this is different from previous technologies.
sentences.zh: 好了，在我们探讨人工智能带来的其他环境问题的一些细节之前，首先有必要花几分钟时间精确澄清一下我们在谈论什么、人工智能是如何消耗能量的，以及这与以往的技术有什么不同。

sentences.en: For starters, using any kind of technology uses energy.
sentences.zh: 首先，使用任何种类的技术都要消耗能量。

sentences.en: When you send an email, search for something on Google, listen to this podcast, or do almost anything that connects to the Internet, information is being transferred between your computer and somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 当你发送电子邮件、在谷歌上搜索东西、听这个播客，或者做任何连接互联网的事情时，信息实际上正在你的电脑和某个其他地方之间传输。

sentences.en: That “somewhere else” isn’t a mysterious cloud floating above your head.
sentences.zh: 那个“其他地方”并不是漂浮在你头顶上的神秘云端。

sentences.en: In most cases, it's a physical location called a data centre.
sentences.zh: 在大多数情况下，它是一个被称为数据中心的物理场所。

sentences.en: A data centre is, essentially, a giant warehouse full of computers, tens of thousands of them, all stacked up in metal racks, blinking away, processing and storing data.
sentences.zh: 数据中心本质上是一个摆满计算机的巨大仓库，里面有几万台计算机，全都在金属架上层层叠叠地码好，一闪一闪地处理和存储数据。

sentences.en: They don’t look very exciting, but they are the backbone of the modern digital world.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来不怎么起眼，但它们是现代数字世界的顶梁柱。

sentences.en: Every photo you upload, every YouTube video you watch, every Spotify song you play, this is all being sent to and from one of these data centres somewhere in the world.
sentences.zh: 你上传的每一张照片、观看的每一个 YouTube 视频、播放的每一首 Spotify 歌曲，其实都在被发送到世界上某个地方的数据中心，或者从那里发送出来。

sentences.en: And all of this takes energy. Your computer or mobile phone needs energy to make the request, so you charge it up at home.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都需要能量。你的电脑或手机需要能量来发出请求，所以你在家里给它充电。

sentences.en: And the computers in the data centre, of course, also need energy; they need electricity.
sentences.zh: 当然，数据中心里的计算机也需要能量；它们需要电力。

sentences.en: But, like any computer, they can also get very hot, which means they need to be cooled; sometimes this is by enormous air-conditioning systems, or in some cases, by water that flows through pipes to remove heat.
sentences.zh: 但和任何计算机一样，它们也会变得很热，这意味着它们需要冷却；有时是通过巨大的空调系统，或者在某些情况下，通过在管道中流动以带走热量的水。

sentences.en: So, whether it’s these air-conditioning systems or cold water, these data centres require large amounts of electricity to keep everything running, and more importantly, to keep everything cool.
sentences.zh: 所以，无论是这些空调系统还是冷水，这些数据中心都需要大量的电力来维持一切运转，更重要的是，维持一切凉爽。

sentences.en: So, even before we get to the question of AI, every time you open a web page, watch a YouTube video, and yes, even listen to a podcast, a little bit of energy is being used somewhere in the world to make that happen.
sentences.zh: 因此，甚至在我们讨论人工智能问题之前，每当你打开一个网页、观看一个 YouTube 视频，甚至是听播客时，世界上的某个地方都在消耗一点点能量来让这一切发生。

sentences.en: Now, with Artificial Intelligence, things are a bit different.
sentences.zh: 而对于人工智能，情况则有些不同。

sentences.en: When you ask ChatGPT a question, or generate an image, or use an AI assistant on your phone, it isn’t just retrieving some information from somewhere.
sentences.zh: 当你向 ChatGPT 提问、生成一张图片，或者使用手机上的 AI 助手时，它不仅仅是从某个地方检索一些信息。

sentences.en: It's computing it, creating something new in real time.
sentences.zh: 它是在进行计算，实时创造出新的东西。

sentences.en: This means much more powerful computers are involved, the kind that can do billions or even trillions of calculations per second.
sentences.zh: 这意味着需要更强大的计算机参与进来，那种每秒可以进行数十亿甚至数万亿次计算的计算机。

sentences.en: These chips, or Graphics Processing Units, GPUs for short, they use far more energy than the servers that store your emails or photos.
sentences.zh: 这些芯片，也就是图形处理器（简称 GPU），比那些存储你的电子邮件或照片的服务器消耗的能量要多得多。

sentences.en: And because AI systems are so large, with billions of parameters or virtual “connections” between artificial neurons, they need vast amounts of energy both to train them and to run them.
sentences.zh: 而且，由于人工智能系统规模如此庞大，拥有数十亿个参数或人工神经元之间的虚拟“连接”，它们无论是训练还是运行都需要大量的能量。

sentences.en: So while a Google search might use enough energy to power a light bulb for a few seconds, generating a single AI image or a long ChatGPT reply, early critics pointed out, might use ten, twenty, or even fifty times more.
sentences.zh: 因此，谷歌搜索可能只消耗足够让灯泡亮几秒钟的能量，而早期批评者指出，生成单张 AI 图片或一条长篇 ChatGPT 回复，可能会消耗十倍、二十倍甚至五十倍的能量。

sentences.en: That is why environmental campaigners have started to pay attention, because AI use is exploding at breakneck speed, and AI is much more energy-intensive than almost every other consumer technology; each request requires far more computing power, therefore more energy.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么环保活动人士开始关注这一点，因为人工智能的使用正以惊人的速度爆炸式增长，而且人工智能比几乎所有其他消费类技术的耗能都要大得多；每一次请求都需要更强大的计算能力，因此需要更多的能量。

sentences.en: But, you are probably wondering, how much energy is this?
sentences.zh: 但是，你可能在想，这到底是多少能量呢？

sentences.en: Well, when ChatGPT was first released, there were all sorts of articles suggesting that it was 22 times more energy-intensive than using Google and that it was a giant menace to the environment.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当 ChatGPT 刚发布时，各种文章都在暗示它的耗能是谷歌的 22 倍，并且它是环境的巨大威胁。

sentences.en: 22 times more emissions sounds bad, but firstly, that number has proved not to be correct, and secondly, it’s important to see it in perspective.
sentences.zh: 排放量增加 22 倍听起来很糟糕，但首先，这个数字后来被证明是不正确的；其次，用客观的眼光来看待它很重要。

sentences.en: On the first point, according to a recent study, a single Google Gemini text query, so a single use of Google’s AI, uses 0.24 Wh of electricity, emits 0.03 grams of CO2, and consumes 0.26 millilitres of water.
sentences.zh: 关于第一点，根据最近的一项研究，单次谷歌 Gemini 文本查询（即单次使用谷歌的 AI）消耗 0.24 瓦时的电力，排放 0.03 克二氧化碳，并消耗 0.26 毫升水。

sentences.en: Now, to put that in perspective, the energy use is like one second of using a microwave, or 6 seconds of having your fridge on.
sentences.zh: 为了让你有个直观的概念，这耗能就像使用微波炉一秒钟，或者让冰箱运行 6 秒钟。

sentences.en: 0.03 grams of CO2 is practically nothing, and 0.26 millilitres is five drops of water.
sentences.zh: 0.03 克的二氧化碳几乎等于没有，而 0.26 毫升就是五滴水。

sentences.en: Now, some AI uses are more intensive, like generating an image or video, and not all AI models are the same; OpenAI, which is the company behind ChatGPT, hasn’t released a similar study, and it’s believed it’s not yet as energy efficient as Google.
sentences.zh: 当然，某些人工智能的用途消耗更大，比如生成图片或视频，而且并非所有的人工智能模型都一样；作为 ChatGPT 背后的公司，OpenAI 尚未发布类似的研究，据信其能效目前还不如谷歌。

sentences.en: I’ll use them semi-interchangeably here.
sentences.zh: 我在这里会交替使用这两个词。

sentences.en: If ChatGPT isn’t yet as efficient as Google Gemini, it will most likely get there shortly, and both will continue to become more, not less, energy-efficient.
sentences.zh: 如果 ChatGPT 的能效目前还不如谷歌 Gemini，它很可能会很快赶上，而且两者的能源利用效率都将持续提高，而不是降低。

sentences.en: So, you’ll excuse me if I flit between the terms.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我在这些术语之间换来换去，还请见谅。

sentences.en: Now, in the interests of balance, there have been some criticisms of this Google study, with commentators pointing out that it doesn’t take into account factors like the training of the AI model or the carbon cost of the AI chips themselves.
sentences.zh: 为了保持客观中立，对这项谷歌研究也有一些批评意见，评论人士指出，它没有将诸如训练人工智能模型或人工智能芯片本身的碳成本等因素考虑在内。

sentences.en: But even taking these into account, the effect is still negligible.
sentences.zh: 但即使把这些考虑进去，其影响仍然微乎其微。

sentences.en: To put it in perspective again, taking everything into account, a single AI query, based on recent estimates, is like uploading 9 photos to social media, leaving a digital alarm clock on for 50 minutes, or streaming Netflix for 30 seconds.
sentences.zh: 为了再次从宏观角度来看，综合考虑所有因素后，根据最近的估计，单次人工智能查询的碳排或能耗相当于在社交媒体上上传 9 张照片、让数字闹钟开着 50 分钟，或者在 Netflix 上观看 30 秒的流媒体视频。

sentences.en: These are things most of us don’t think twice about, yet it is AI that has come under the spotlight.
sentences.zh: 这些都是我们大多数人不会多想的事情，然而被放在聚光灯下的却是人工智能。

sentences.en: The news is full of articles with headlines like “training an AI model is like 550 return flights from New York to San Francisco”, or that “ChatGPT emits as much CO2 as 20,000 American households”.
sentences.zh: 新闻里到处都是这样的头条文章：“训练一个 AI 模型相当于纽约到旧金山的 550 个往返航班”，或者“ChatGPT 排放的二氧化碳相当于 2 万个美国家庭”。

sentences.en: Or, of course, even by the BBC, which should know better, “AI uses 27 million bottles of water in Scotland”.
sentences.zh: 当然，甚至还有 BBC 的文章，明知不该如此却依然发文称：“AI 在苏格兰消耗了 2700 万瓶水”。

sentences.en: Yes, the total energy impact of AI has grown incredibly quickly, but it started from zero.
sentences.zh: 是的，AI 的总体能源影响增长得极其迅速，但它是从零开始的。

sentences.en: ChatGPT went from zero to 100 million users in under a year.
sentences.zh: ChatGPT 在不到一年的时间里，用户数从零飙升至 1 亿。

sentences.en: By July 2025, it had 700 million users, 10% of the world’s adult population, sending 18 billion messages every week.
sentences.zh: 截至 2025 年 7 月，它拥有 7 亿用户，占世界成年人口的 10%，每周发送 180 亿条消息。

sentences.en: Now, those numbers will be higher, and it looks like they will continue to trend up.
sentences.zh: 现在，这些数字还会更高，而且看起来它们将继续呈上升趋势。

sentences.en: Using a tiny amount of energy 18 billion times a week, well, it does add up, and this is part of where the concern comes from.
sentences.zh: 每周有 180 亿次使用微量能量的行为，嗯，这确实积少成多，这也是担忧的来源之一。

sentences.en: But, even when all global AI use is added together, it still doesn’t even add up to a fraction of a per cent.
sentences.zh: 但是，即便把全球所有 AI 的使用量加在一起，它甚至连百分之一都不到。

sentences.en: And to think, this is a technology that is being used by 1 in every 10 adults, voluntarily, I should add.
sentences.zh: 想想看，这是一种被十分之一的成年人自愿使用的技术，我得补充一句。

sentences.en: Sure, ChatGPT or other AI models aren’t perfect, and you might not use them yourself.
sentences.zh: 当然，ChatGPT 或其他 AI 模型并不完美，你可能自己不用它们。

sentences.en: But they can be incredibly helpful, saving you time, making you more productive, and assisting you in a myriad of ways.
sentences.zh: 但它们可以带来难以置信的帮助，为你节省时间、提高工作效率，并以无数种方式协助你。

sentences.en: When you think about it, technology is incredibly efficient in its energy use.
sentences.zh: 仔细想想，技术在能源利用方面是极其高效的。

sentences.en: Every data centre in the world, so that’s the computers powering the entire internet, not just AI, uses 1.5% of the world’s electricity and 0.23% of the world’s energy.
sentences.zh: 世界上每一个数据中心——也就是说，为整个互联网提供动力的计算机，而不仅仅是 AI——消耗了世界 1.5% 的电力和 0.23% 的能源。

sentences.en: And to think, the average person spends six and a half hours per day online, interacting with data centres.
sentences.zh: 想想看，普通人平均每天花六个半小时在线上与数据中心互动。

sentences.en: In many ways, it's a miracle that something that’s now so fundamental to our lives has such a tiny environmental impact.
sentences.zh: 从很多方面来看，一个对我们的生活如此基础的事物却对环境产生如此微小的影响，简直是一个奇迹。

sentences.en: And of course, if we are to compare any of these technological uses to “offline” energy uses, the difference is even more pronounced.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果我们把任何这些技术应用与“离线”能源使用进行比较，这种差异就更加明显了。

sentences.en: Producing one burger requires around 2,000 litres of water, enough to run almost 10 million Google Gemini queries, nearly 300 a day, for 100 years.
sentences.zh: 生产一个汉堡需要大约 2000 升水，这些水足够支撑近 1000 万次谷歌 Gemini 查询，也就是差不多每天 300 次，连续用 100 年。

sentences.en: Now, this is not for me to say you should stop eating burgers or never take an aeroplane again; that’s not my point.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说你应该停止吃汉堡或者再也不坐飞机了；这不是我的观点。

sentences.en: Rather, it’s that to think that you should restrict your personal use of ChatGPT, but still go to McDonald’s is like deciding you’re going to cycle to take a private plane; it is wildly misunderstanding the impact of the two activities.
sentences.zh: 相反，我的意思是，如果你认为自己应该限制个人对 ChatGPT 的使用，却依然去吃麦当劳，那就好比你决定骑自行车去赶私人飞机；这完全是对这两种行为影响的严重误解。

sentences.en: But there is one point that’s worth pointing out, and that is relating to the type of energy that’s used in these data centres.
sentences.zh: 不过，有一点值得指出，那就是这些数据中心所使用能源的类型。

sentences.en: When you use ChatGPT or any other model, your query is typically routed to the nearest data centre to you.
sentences.zh: 当你使用 ChatGPT 或任何其他模型时，你的查询通常会被路由到离你最近的数据中心。

sentences.en: The environmental impact of each request is largely dependent on the type of energy used to power that data centre.
sentences.zh: 每次请求对环境的影响很大程度上取决于为该数据中心供电的能源类型。

sentences.en: And given the heavy electricity requirements, these data centres are often powered by dirtier energy sources such as coal or oil.
sentences.zh: 鉴于巨大的电力需求，这些数据中心通常由煤炭或石油等较为污染环境的能源提供动力。

sentences.en: This is part of the reason technology companies are busy pledging to switch to cleaner energy sources —not necessarily because they have some inherent love for the environment, but because the cleaner the energy used in their data centres, the less ammunition environmental critics have against them.
sentences.zh: 这也是科技公司忙于承诺转向清洁能源的部分原因——不一定是因为它们天生热爱环境，而是因为数据中心使用的能源越清洁，环保批评者针对它们的弹药就越少。

sentences.en: And there’s more. Water use might be a non-issue in the wet and rainy country of Scotland, but in countries less blessed by constant showers and flowing rivers, it is.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此。在湿润多雨的苏格兰，水资源利用可能不是个问题，但在那些没有经常下雨和流淌河流眷顾的国家里，它就是个问题。

sentences.en: Whether that’s in the Middle East or in Arizona, every litre of water that goes to a data centre is a litre of water that isn’t available for something else.
sentences.zh: 无论是中东还是亚利桑那州，流入数据中心的每一升水，都是无法用于其他用途的一升水。

sentences.en: And the sheer scale of the growth in AI, and the data centres required for this, is mindboggling.
sentences.zh: 人工智能增长的绝对规模，以及为此所需的数据中心，简直令人匪夷所思。

sentences.en: By some estimates, the energy demand from data centres is set to double by 2030, with half of this growth driven by AI.
sentences.zh: 据估计，到 2030 年，数据中心的能源需求将翻一番，其中一半的增长是由人工智能驱动的。

sentences.en: And “personal” AI use is just a slice of this.
sentences.zh: 而“个人”人工智能的使用只是其中的一小部分。

sentences.en: By personal AI use, I mean an individual, you or me, or any of the other hundreds of millions of people using ChatGPT or other AI tools, and going into the interface and asking a question.
sentences.zh: 我所说的个人人工智能使用，是指个人（你我，或者使用 ChatGPT 或其他 AI 工具的其他数亿人中的任何一个）进入界面并提出问题。

sentences.en: There is also all of the behind-the-scenes use of AI by companies, whether that’s companies using AI models for their internal business processes or it’s the AI companies themselves.
sentences.zh: 此外，还有公司在幕后对 AI 的各种使用，无论是企业将 AI 模型用于其内部业务流程，还是 AI 公司本身。

sentences.en: So even if you never choose to use AI tools personally, every time you interact with a technology company, you will most probably be using some form of AI, whether you like it or not.
sentences.zh: 因此，即便你从不选择亲自使用 AI 工具，每当你与科技公司互动时，无论你是否愿意，你很可能都在使用某种形式的 AI。

sentences.en: So, to wrap things up, global AI use is probably at the lowest it will ever be in your or my lifetime.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，全球 AI 的能源消耗可能处于你我一生中的最低点。

sentences.en: New models are coming out almost every week, adoption is increasing fast, and AI is being deployed into everything we do.
sentences.zh: 几乎每周都有新模型问世，普及速度正在加快，AI 正在被部署到我们所做的每一件事中。

sentences.en: Yes, it might use significantly more energy than things like traditional Google searches, but it is far from the worst thing you can do with a computer, and its environmental impact pales in comparison with most things you do in the real world.
sentences.zh: 是的，它消耗的能量可能明显多于传统谷歌搜索等事物，但它远非你用电脑能做出的最糟糕的事情，而且它的环境影响与你在现实世界中所做的大多数事情相比简直不值一提。

sentences.en: And the good news is that AI is getting much more energy-efficient, with that Google study reporting that energy use for each query is now 3% of what it was a year ago, a 33-fold reduction.
sentences.zh: 好消息是，AI 的能效正在变得更高，那项谷歌研究报告称，现在每次查询的能源消耗是去年的 3%，即减少了 33 倍。

sentences.en: Yes, AI does have an impact on the environment, but on an individual level, it offers a miraculous reward for a minuscule environmental cost.
sentences.zh: 是的，AI 确实对环境有影响，但在个人层面，它以微乎其微的环境成本带来了奇迹般的回报。

sentences.en: When it comes to reducing your personal carbon footprint, there are dozens of lifestyle changes, such as flying less and taking public transport, that would have a vastly greater impact than your personal use of AI.
sentences.zh: 说到减少你的个人碳足迹，有几十种生活方式的改变，比如少坐飞机和乘坐公共交通，其影响将远大于你个人对 AI 的使用。

sentences.en: So, it's up to you, but if you ask me whether I’d prefer to skip one burger, or not use AI again for the rest of my life, I think you can guess what I would say.
sentences.zh: 所以，这取决于你，但如果你问我是愿意少吃一个汉堡，还是这辈子再也不用 AI，我想你能猜到我会怎么说。

sentences.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode on the environmental impact on AI.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天的关于 AI 环境影响的节目就到这里。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 希望这期节目对你有所启发，让你学到了新知识。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know what you thought of this episode.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我很想知道你对这期节目的看法。

sentences.en: What had you heard about the environmental impact of AI?
sentences.zh: 关于 AI 对环境的影响，你以前听过什么？

sentences.en: Had you changed your behaviour, or will you change your behaviour after listening to this?
sentences.zh: 听完这期节目后，你改变了自己的行为吗？或者你会改变吗？

sentences.en: I would love to know. Let me know in the comments below if you're listening to this somewhere where you can comment, and for the members among you, you can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道。如果你在可以评论的地方收听这期节目，请在下方的评论区告诉我；至于我们的会员朋友，你可以直接进入我们的社区论坛（网址是 community.leonardoenglish.com），和其他充满好奇心的人一起畅聊。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你刚才收听的是由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，请注意安全，我们下期节目见。
